clue.text: Start to swiftly forget when heated romance breaks off? On the contrary

definitions.text: Start to swiftly forget when heated romance breaks off? On the contrary

parts.words: Start to swiftly forget when heated romance breaks off? On the contrary
parts.note: the question describes forgetting a lover once apart; 'On the contrary' flips it into the old proverb that time apart deepens love

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether passion fades fast once an affair ends, then suggests the opposite is true.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 26 across. Reverse every idea in the question (forget becomes grow fonder, breaking off becomes being apart) and the familiar saying appears.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb claims that separation strengthens affection, the exact opposite of quickly forgetting a lost lover.

clue.text: Having many weapons, met death or explosive force

indicators.note: something explosive blows apart, so the letters of these three words are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: teeth means force or real power, as when a law is said to have teeth

explanation.surface: A grim line about meeting death or facing an explosive force, fittingly on the theme of heavy weaponry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosive' rearranges MET DEATH OR into ARMEDTOTHE; 'force' then gives TEETH.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone carrying a large arsenal of guns and other arms.

clue.text: Band leader leaving instruments in southeast capital

indicators.note: the shortened instruments sit inside the abbreviation for southeast

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast

indicators.note: leaving means the band's leading letter departs from the instruments

parts.note: banjos are stringed instruments

indicators.note: the leader of Band is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bandleader walks out on the group's instruments somewhere in a south-eastern capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' picks the first letter of Band, which 'leaving' drops; 'in' sets what is left between the two compass letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of Costa Rica in Central America.

clue.text: Make changes to scenery as required

indicators.note: making changes to the letters means reordering them into a new word

explanation.surface: A stage director asks for the scenery to be altered as needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something required is needed or essential, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Journalist penning military base's exploits, initially

definitions.text: Journalist penning military base's exploits, initially

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the editor's letters wrap around the initials

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the usual crossword journalist

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A reporter writes up what is happening at an army base, as a war correspondent might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives M, B and E, which ED encloses. The whole clue also describes the answer: a reporter attached to a military unit writing about its exploits.
explanation.definitionFit: An embed is a reporter attached to a military unit, living with the troops to cover a campaign.

clue.text: Emergency service doctors backing universal clean up

indicators.note: backing means the abbreviation for the doctors' body is written backwards

parts.note: the BMA is the British Medical Association, the doctors' professional body
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal
to lance a boil or wound is to cut it open and clean it out

explanation.surface: Medics support a universal clean-up drive, a fittingly medical picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns BMA into AMB.
explanation.definitionFit: This vehicle and its crew answer emergency calls, taking the sick and injured to hospital.

clue.text: Independent carrying news during European Union malaise

indicators.note: during puts the news letters within the pair of letters for the union

parts.note: N stands for new, so two Ns stand for news, more than one new thing
I is the abbreviation for independent; in a down entry it carries the other letters, sitting beneath them

explanation.surface: An independent newspaper reports on gloom spreading through the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light the I sits at the foot, so it is pictured carrying the rest on its back, which is why it comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a weariness of spirit akin to a general malaise.

clue.text: Wave off model — special single friend from France

parts.note: the Model T was the classic Ford car
in French un means one, a single, and ami means friend

explanation.surface: Someone waves goodbye to a model and a special single French friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from France' applies to both 'single' and 'friend', giving the French UN and AMI.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave triggered by an earthquake or landslide.

clue.text: Run crucial works around old city — right outside of course

parts.note: in cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters wrap the old city
works signals that the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An instruction to run important works around an ancient city, setting the right course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' rearranges the fodder as CRICULA, and 'around' wraps that round the old city after its first C. An extra is a cricket run not scored off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Extracurricular activities lie beyond the regular programme of study, outside the set syllabus.

clue.text: Small car — one reserved by radio?

definitions.meaning: a modest little taxi car of the private-hire kind
private-hire taxis must be booked in advance, traditionally dispatched over the radio

explanation.surface: A small car, perhaps one kept aside for radio use.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is a private-hire taxi: unlike a black cab it cannot be hailed on the street and has to be booked ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a private-hire taxi that is ordered by phone and sent out by its office over the radio.

clue.text: Make illegal journey wanting society dinner with royalty?

parts.note: to ban something is to make it illegal

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the society letter is dropped

parts.note: a quest is a long journey or search

explanation.surface: Someone travels illicitly to avoid a society dinner attended by royals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' removes S from QUEST to leave QUET.
explanation.definitionFit: A state banquet is a grand formal meal, the kind hosted by a monarch, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Key to short game over ditches

parts.note: D is a musical key

indicators.note: over signals that the cut-down game is turned back to front
short means the last letter of the game is cut off

parts.note: a sport is a game

explanation.surface: Advice on the key to a quick game, played out over ditches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts SPORT to SPOR, and 'over' turns that into ROPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop someone or something is to abandon it, just as one ditches a plan or partner.

clue.text: A country boy returning without adult religious leader

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the reversed letters surround the adult letter
returning means the run of a, country and boy is read backwards

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
a lad is a boy
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A rural boy comes home with no grown-up and meets a spiritual figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the first three pieces into DALILAMA; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so that string goes round the adult letter.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhism, a leading religious figure.

clue.text: Drama with one in fashion business

parts.note: an opera is a sung drama

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for fashionable society

parts.note: the ton is an old word for fashionable society or the height of fashion
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Theatre combined with a fashion company makes a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ton' is a dated term for high fashion and the fashionable set; 'in' puts I inside it to give TION.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation can mean a business or enterprise, as in a large retail operation.

clue.text: English court framed by corrupt prison officer

indicators.note: framed by means set inside, with the jumbled prison letters forming the border
corrupt suggests the letters are spoiled and reordered

explanation.surface: An English court is stitched up by a crooked jail officer, a story of corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges the jail word as INSPOR, and 'framed by' sets the English court letters in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is a police officer of rank above sergeant.

clue.text: Pass on gold rings as valedictory offering

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so the gold symbol goes around the word for passing on

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to pass on is to die

explanation.surface: Handing over gold rings as a parting gift.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a French-derived farewell, words offered when saying goodbye.

clue.text: Not keen on tagliatelle? Ultimately, there's nothing for a starter

parts.note: to be anti something is to be against it, not keen on it

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the pasta, which is replaced

parts.note: tagliatelle is an example of pasta, hence the question mark
O is the zero shape, nothing

explanation.surface: A diner who dislikes ribbon pasta concludes there is nothing to order as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately, there's nothing for a' swaps the last A of PASTA for O, giving PASTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian appetiser course served before the pasta, a starter.

clue.text: Attractive female cyclist winning races?

indicators.note: winning in the sense of capturing, so the cyclist takes the races inside him

parts.note: Sir Chris Hoy is a British Olympic champion track cyclist
the TT, or Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race series

explanation.surface: A glamorous woman cyclist who keeps winning races.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Hoy is a Scottish track cyclist with six Olympic golds; the TT is the Isle of Man motorbike races.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal slang for a sexy, good-looking person, especially a woman.

clue.text: Lofted a shot to test draw

indicators.note: lofted means raised up, so in this down entry the pieces read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lob is a high shot in tennis
the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles

explanation.surface: A tennis player hits a high shot to test the opponent, ending in a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lofted' sends A LOB MOT upwards, giving TOMBOLA. The MOT is Britain's yearly roadworthiness test for cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a raffle-style lottery in which tickets are drawn from a revolving drum.

clue.text: Observer odds against to react badly

parts.note: SP, the starting price, is the betting odds on a horse at the off

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put together wrongly, in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A punter's odds turn against them and they react poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges TO REACT as ECTATOR. SP is the bookmakers' starting price.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is someone who watches an event, an onlooker.

clue.text: Much, much more to loveless embrace

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, so loveless means the round letter is removed

parts.note: to enfold is to wrap in the arms, to embrace

explanation.surface: A plea for far more than a loveless hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' drops O (love, zero in tennis) from TO, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenfold means ten times as great, so vastly more than before.

clue.text: Magazine article for Apple Watch?

parts.note: Time is the American news magazine
a piece is a written article

explanation.surface: A magazine runs a feature about the Apple Watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple Watch' is one example of the type, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Any watch or clock is a timepiece, and Apple's smartwatch is one brand-name example.

clue.text: Describe old man wearing shirt?

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
in means dressed in, as in a man in a suit
a T-shirt is a kind of shirt, so the letter T stands for one

explanation.surface: Asking someone to describe an elderly man dressed in a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint a picture in words is to describe, as in painting someone as a villain.

clue.text: Finance seen regularly on familiar US index

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word seen

parts.note: the Dow, short for the Dow Jones, is the well-known American stock index

explanation.surface: A financial picture seen regularly on a well-known American market index.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of SEEN, E and N; in this down light they sit on top of DOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow an institution is to fund it with a permanent gift of money.

clue.text: Copper arresting drunk in a flap

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the police letters hold the jumbled pair

parts.note: PC is a police constable, a copper

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A police officer arrests a drunk who is in a state of agitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges IN A as ANI.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a flap is to be in a state of panic or agitation.

clue.text: Self-important person, say, first to back bars

indicators.note: bars as in prison bars, which shut something in, so the letters go inside

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as say does
first is written 1ST, and the digit one is read as the letter I

indicators.note: back means the little word to is turned around

explanation.surface: A conceited person is, say, the first to support the bars.
explanation.walkthrough: EG plus IST (1ST, first) holds OT, which 'back' makes from TO.
explanation.definitionFit: An egotist is a conceited person who thinks and talks mostly about themselves.

clue.text: Strip of French land including left bank in Paris

parts.note: de is the French word for of

indicators.note: including means the land contains the letter for left

parts.note: soil is land or earth
port is the left side, and P stands for port, the way a ship or plane banks to the left

explanation.surface: A strip of French territory containing Paris's famous Left Bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rive Gauche picture is a decoy: 'in Paris' simply backs up the French DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To despoil a place is to strip it of its valuables, to plunder it.

clue.text: See 1
